en: הַר, (הֶרֶר) m. (Biblical Hebrew; הרר) mound, mountain; trnsf. eminent person. Middot II, 1, and from הַר הבית the Temple mount. Yevamot 17ᵃ (play on ה̇ר̇פ̇נ̇יא) ה̇ר̇ שהכל פ̇ונ̇ין בו a hill to which all turn (whose spurious descent prevents them from getting wives elsewhere); and see from—Chullin 39ᵇ (in Chald. diction) רישיך והר here is thy head and here the mountain (a colloquial phrase for compelling one to give up a bargain).—Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 28 (reference. to Shemot XIX, 3) בזכות הה׳ for the merit of the distinguished one (Abraham), ואין הה׳ אלא אבות har means the patriarchs (reference. to Micah VI, 2). Sanhedrin 107ᵃ ה׳ שבכם the most prominent of you; and from—[For proper nouns composed with הר, see respective determinants.]—plural הָרִים, הֲרָרִים. Tamid 32ᵃ, and e. הָרֵי חושך, see חו̇שֶׁךְ.—Sanhedrin 24ᵃ עוקר הרי הרים uprooting the highest mountains (a figure for dialectical ingenuity). Yerushalmi Yevamot I, 3ᵃ bottom of page בין שני הֶהָ׳ וכ׳ between the two high mountains (great scholars). Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 15 ואין ה׳ אלא אבות, see supra.—Chagigah I, 8 כה׳ תלויין בשערה like mountains suspended on a hair (a slender Bible text for numerous Talmudic laws); and see from

comments.en: Mount Moriah, the Temple Mount, measured 500 cubits by 500 cubits. It was surrounded by a wall. [The earth beneath it was hollowed out to prevent contracting ritual impurity] due to Tumat Ohel. Arches above arches were built underneath [for support]. It was entirely covered, one colonnade inside another.
comments.he: הַר הַבַּיִת וְהוּא הַר הַמּוֹרִיָּה הָיָה חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת אַמָּה עַל חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת אַמָּה וְהָיָה מֻקָּף חוֹמָה. וְכֵפִין עַל גַּבֵּי כֵּפִין הָיוּ בְּנוּיוֹת מִתַּחְתָּיו. מִפְּנֵי אֹהֶל הַטֻּמְאָה. וְכֻלּוֹ הָיָה מְקֹרֶה סְטָיו לְפָנִים מִסְּטָיו:

comments.en: Of this, a square measuring a full 500 by 500 shall be reserved for the Sanctuary, and 50 cubits for an open space all around it.
comments.he: יִֽהְיֶ֤ה מִזֶּה֙ אֶל־הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֛וֹת בַּחֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת מְרֻבָּ֣ע סָבִ֑יב וַחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אַמָּ֔ה מִגְרָ֥שׁ ל֖וֹ סָבִֽיב׃

sections.en: The Temple Mount was five hundred cubits by five hundred cubits. The greater part of it was on the south; next to that on the east; next to that on the north; and the smallest part on the west. The part which was most extensive was the part most used.
sections.he: הַר הַבַּיִת הָיָה חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת אַמָּה עַל חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת אַמָּה, רֻבּוֹ מִן הַדָּרוֹם, שֵׁנִי לוֹ מִן הַמִּזְרָח, שְׁלִישִׁי לוֹ מִן הַצָּפוֹן, מִעוּטוֹ מִן הַמַּעֲרָב. מְקוֹם שֶׁהָיָה רֹב מִדָּתוֹ, שָׁם הָיָה רֹב תַּשְׁמִישׁוֹ:

en:
נָחַם (Biblical Hebrew; compare נוּחַ) to be at ease. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 20 (homiletic interpret. of נָחָם, Shemot XIII, 17) אמר הקב"ה איני מתנחם וכ׳ the Lord said, I shall not be contented, until &c., for we read ולא נָחַם (perhaps meant for נִחַם Nifal).

Piël - נִיחֵם to comfort, console. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Naḥ., p. 128ᵃ א"ל הקב"ה אני ואתם נלך ונְנַחֲמֶנָּה the Lord said to them (the prophets), Myself and you, let us go and comfort her (Jerusalem); ib. נַחֲמוּהָ עמי וכ׳ comfort her, O my people; comfort her, you on high (angels) &c. Ib. הקב"ה שלחני אצלך לנַחֲמֵךְ the Lord sent me to thee (Jerusalem) to comfort thee. Ib.ᵇ נַחֲמוּנִי נחמוני עמי comfort me, comfort me, O my people. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 30 ונכנסו חביריו לנַחֲמוֹ and his friends came in to comfort him; אם על אשתו מְנַחֲמִים לו וכ׳ if it is for the loss of his wife that they seek to console him, and he refuses to be consoled &c. Middot II, 2 השוכן בבית הזה יְנַחֶמְךָ may He who resides in this house console thee. Yerushalmi Gittin V, 47ᶜ top; Yerushalmi Demai IV, 24ᵃ bottom of page ומְנַחֲמִין אבילי וכ׳ and you must comfort the gentile mourners (of your place) as well as the Jewish mourners; Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. I, 39ᶜ bottom of page ניחמים (correct accordingly); Tosefta Gittin V (III), 5; and from—מְנַחֵם the consoling friend of the mourner. Yalkut Mishlei 947 בבית האבל בחול פריס מנ׳ ויהיב לאבל … יש לה מנ׳ פריס מנ׳ וכ׳ in the house of the mourner, on week days, the comforter breaks the bread and gives it to the mourner, as it is written (Eicha I, 17), ‘Zion breaks (the bread) with her own hands, she has no comforter’, but if she had a comforter, the comforter would break it &c.—plural מְנַחֲמִים, מְנַחֲמִין. Moʿed Katan 27ᵃ בית המנ׳ the room where the comforters meet. Ib. 27ᵇ כיון שניענע … אין מנ׳ וכ׳ as soon as the mourner nods with his head (indicating that he accepts their consolations), the friends are no longer permitted to sit with him; and from—Shabbat 152ᵃ מת שאין לו מנ׳ a deceased person that leaves no direct relations to be comforted.

Nifal - נִחַם,

Hithpaël - הִתְנַחֵם, , Nithpaël נִתְנַחֵם
1) to be comforted, accept consolation. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana l. common gender. מי צריך להִנָּחֵם which of them is in need of being comforted?; ib. להִתְנַחֵם. Sanhedrin 19ᵃ תִּתְנֶחָמוּ be comforted. Ib. מִתְנַחֵם מאחרים receiving consolations from others. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. l. common gender. ואינו מתנחם, see supra. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 84 מִתְנַחֲמִים על המתים וכ׳ people accept consolation for dead persons but not for living ones (that have disappeared); and from—Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 27 (explained וינחם, Breishit VI, 6) מתנ׳ אני שבראתי וכ׳ I have that consolation that I created him (man) to live on earth below &c.

—2) to seek comfort; to be sorry, regret, reconsider. Ib. מתנ׳ אני שעשיתו וכ׳ I regret that I made him, and that he was placed on earth. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 45, beginning ואני מתנ׳ עליו and I am sorry for him (reconsider my judgment). Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 23 (reference. to Bamidbar XXIII, 19) לא בן עמרם עשה אותו להִנָּחֵם did not the son of Amram cause him (God) to reconsider (Shemot XXXII, 14); ib. להִתְנַחֵם; Yerushalmi Taanit I, 65ᵇ bottom of page שעשה לאל שיִתְנֶחָם; and from

עָבַר (Biblical Hebrew)
1) to be thick, swell; to run over. Parah VI, 4 כדי שׁיַעַבְרוּ המים וכ׳ that the water may overflow into a vessel; and e.—Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 15 שאני עוֹבֵר, see עֶבְרָה.

—2) (compare סְגֵי I and II) to pass, to cross. Tosefta Sotah VIII, 1; Sotah 33ᵇ כיצד עָבְרוּ ישראל את וכ׳ in what manner did the Israelites cross the Jordan? Shir HaShirim Rabbah to V, 13 עוֹבֵר הוא וחוזר וכ׳ he goes over his studies once and again &c.; and from—ע׳ את הדין to cross the line of justice, to be too severe. Middot II, 2 כאילו עברו עליו וכ׳ as if they had treated him too severely (arbitrarily). Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 30 כשם שאני יכול לַעֲבוֹר … ואני איני מַעֲבִיר וכ׳ as I (the Lord) have power to treat the nations with rigor, but refrain from doing so, so shall you not go beyond the line of justice. Ib. עִיבְּרָה את הדין (Piël); and e.

—3) (with על) to pass over (a sin); to forgive. Shir HaShirim Rabbah to V, 5 (play on מור עובר, ib.) מר עובר ע׳ על מררי the bitterness passes away, he (the Lord) passes over my bitterness (sin). Rosh Hashanah 17ᵃ (reference. to Micah VII, 18) למי נושא עון למי שעובר על פשע whose iniquity does he pardon? the iniquity of him who forgives (his neighbor’s) transgression; and e.

—4) to transgress, sin. Yoma 86ᵇ, and e. כיון שע׳ אדם עבירה ושנה וכ׳ as soon as a man has committed a sin and repeated it, it becomes to him a permitted act. Ib. 86ᵃ, and e. ע׳ על עשה when one has transgressed a positive law (committed a sin of omission). Ib. ע׳ על כריתות וכ׳ when one has committed sins punishable with extinction or death by a court. Eruvin 100ᵃ, and from עובר על בל וכ׳, see בַּל. Ketubot VII, 6 העוֹבֶרֶת על דת וכ׳ if a wife offends against Mosaic or Jewish customs, see דַּת; Yerushalmi ib. VII, 31ᶜ top נשים המְעַבְּרוֹת על הדת (Piël); and see from

—5) to pass, overtake, precede. Pesachim 7ᵇ כל המצות מברך עליהן עובר לעשייתן in the performance of all religious ceremonies one must say the benediction over them before doing them; מאי משמע דהאי עובר לישנא דאקדומי היא what evidence is there that this ‘ober has the meaning of precedence? Answ. by reference. to ויעבר (II Samuel XVIII, 23) ‘and he arrived before the Cushite’.

—6) to pass by, go away, be removed. Pesachim III, 1 אלו עוֹבְרִין בפסח the following things must pass away (their use must be suspended) during Passover. Beitzah 26ᵃ, and from מום עובר a transitory blemish, opposed קבוע. Berakhot 26ᵃ ע׳ יומו בטל קרבנו when its day is passed, the sacrifice of the day is void. Pesachim II, 2 חמץ … שע׳ עליו הפסח leavened matter … over which Passover has passed (which had been in the house during Passover). Berakhot IX, 3 הצועק לַשֶּׁעָבַר וכ׳ praying for what is passed (decided) is a vain prayer, e.g. if one’s wife is with child, and one prays, may it be the will of God that my wife bear a male child; Yerushalmi Taanit II, 65ᶜ bottom of page נותן הודייה לשעבר וצועק וכ׳ one gives thanks for what is passed, and prays for what is to come. Gittin VII, 7 כל זמן שאֱעֶבוֹר מכנגד פניך וכ׳ as soon as I shall have been out of thy sight for thirty days; Tosefta ib. VII (V), 10. Ketubot 17ᵃ ע׳ מלפני כלה he passed aside to make room for a bridal procession. Yoma 66ᵃ, and e. חטאת שעָבְרָה שנתה a sin-offering whose year is passed (that is older than one year); Temurah 22ᵃ שעִיבְּרָה שנתה (Piël) whose year is completed (see infra). Ib. 21ᵇ בכור שעברה שנתו a first-born animal older than one year; Rosh Hashanah 5ᵇ; Zevachim 29ᵃ bottom of page שעיברה; Tosefta Sanhedrin III, 6 בכור שעיברה זמנו ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (read with Variant: שעבר). Ketubot 87ᵃ על שֶׁעָ׳ as regards the past, see עָתִיד; and see from—לַשֶּׁעָ׳ in former days. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 47, opposed עַכְשָׁיו; and from

Hifil - הֶעֱבִיר
1) to lead past, stroke gently. Tosefta Shabbat VII (VIII), 23 [read:] מַעֲבִירִין על גבי העין בשבת you are permitted to stroke a sore eye on the Sabbath; Yerushalmi ib. XIV, 14ᶜ bottom of page מעבירין על העין. Ib. הֶעֱבִירוּ עליו כלים they passed garments over it.

—2) to cause to pass; to remove, displace. Ketubot 17ᵃ מַעֲבִירִין את המת מלפני כלה וכ׳ a funeral procession is made to make way for a bridal procession, and both of them for the king, see supra. Gittin 57ᵇ שאין אנו מעבירין אותו באל אחר that we shall never displace him for another god; שאין מַעֲבִיר אותנו וכ׳ that he will never displace us for another nation. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 30 כאילו היא מעביר איקינין וכ׳ as if he removed (defaced) the king’s portrait; and from

—3) to go beyond. Ib. איני מעביר וכ׳, see supra. Ib. הבריות מעבירין על הדין וכ׳ men go beyond the line of justice (are treacherous, cruel), and they are punished; and e.

—4) to skip over; to forego, postpone.—ה׳ על מדותיו, see מִדָּה.—Yoma 33ᵃ; 58ᵇ, and from אין מעבירין על המצות you must not forego the occasion for performing a religious act. Eruvin 64ᵇ אין מעבירין על האוכלין you must not pass by eatables (and let them lie in the street); Bava Metzia 23ᵃ; and from

—5) to forego, overlook, pardon. Rosh Hashanah 17ᵃ (reference. to Micah VII, 18) מעביר ראשון ראשין וכך היא המדה (Manuscript Munich על ראשון וכ׳; see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note) he pardons one sin after the other (before they are put on the scale), and such is the divine dealing. Ib. מעבירין לו על כל פשעיו all his transgressions are pardoned; and from

—6) to cause to forego or disregard. Eruvin 41ᵇ שלשה דברים מעבירין … על וכ׳ three things make a man disregard his own sense (of right) and the sense of his Maker; and e.

Piël - עִיבֵּר
1) to be completed, full. Temurah 22ᵃ, and e., see supra.

—2) to transgress repeatedly. Yerushalmi Ketubot VII, 31ᶜ top, see supra.

—3) to go beyond. Shemot Rabbah l. common gender. עיברה את הדין, see supra. [Tosefta Bava Kamma VI, 22 שעיברה הדליקה עד, read with Yerushalmi ib. VII, 5ᶜ. שעברה … את.]

—4) (see עוּבָּר) to carry, be with young. Kiddushin 31ᵇ כי עִבַּרְתּוֹ אמו וכ׳ while his mother was pregnant with him, his father died. Tosefta Bava Kamma X, 1 ועִיבְּרָה אצלו (Bava Kamma IX, 1 ונִתְעַבְּרָה) and the cow became pregnant while she was in his possession. Chullin 58ᵃ; and from—Part. pass. f. מְעוּבֶּרֶת; plural מְעוּבָּרוֹת pregnant. Yevamot XVI, 1. Ib. 36ᵇ, and e. מע׳ חבירו a woman who is with child of another man (divorced or widowed during pregnancy). Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 85 מלכים אני מע׳ גואלים אני מע׳ I am pregnant with kings, with redeemers (kings and redeemers are destined to be of my offspring). Yevamot III, 10
; and from—4) (see עִיבּוּר) to extend the city limits, for the purpose of defining Sabbath distances, in cases of buildings projecting beyond the city lines (outskirts). Eruvin V, 1 כיצד מְעַבְּרִין וכ׳ (see אָבַר), defined ib. 53ᵃ; Yerushalmi ib. V, beginning 22ᵇ; Yerushalmi Berakhot VII, 12ᶜ top כאשה עוברה like a pregnant woman; Tosefta Berakhot VI (V), 1; and e.—6) to complement, add to, especially to intercalate a month, (second Adar); proclaim a leap year; to complement a month (see מָלֵא) by assigning to it an additional day (thirty days). Tosefta Sanhedrin II, 1 שנים אומרים צריכה לְעַבֵּר if two judges say, it is necessary to intercalate a month. Ib. 2 על שלשה סימנים מעברין וכ׳ on three indications the intercalation is decided; על שנים מעברין וכ׳ when two of them exist, the intercalation is decreed. Ib. ואם עִיבְּרוּהָ הרי זו מעוברת but if they proclaimed it a leap-year, it remains a leap-year; and from—Part. pass. מְעוּבָּר; f. מְעוּבֶּרֶת. Rosh Hashanah 19ᵇ אלול מע׳ an Elul of thirty days. Sanhedrin 11ᵇ אינה מע׳ the year is not a leap-year (the declared intercalation is invalid); and from

Hithpaël - הִתְעַבֵּר,

Nithpaël - נִתְעַבֵּר
1) to swell (with anger), to become wroth. Sifré Bamidbar 135 (explained ויתעבר, Devarim III, 26) כאדם שאומר נ׳ בי פלוני נתמלא וכ׳ as a man says, that man (became full) got wroth with me, meaning, he was filled with wrath against me; Yalkut Devarim 818; Sifré Devarim 29 כאשה שאינה יכולה לשוח מפני עוברה (swelled,) like a woman that cannot bend down on account of the child she is pregnant with; see עֶבְרָה.

—2) to become pregnant. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 45 מביאה … נִתְעַבְּרָה she conceived on her first intercourse; אין אשה מִתְעַבֶּרֶת וכ׳ no woman conceives on &c.; Yevamot 34ᵃ. Ib. 34ᵇ כדי שלא תִתְעַבֵּר וכ׳ that she may not become with child, and her beauty &c., see כָּחַשׁ. Bava Kamma IX, 1 ונתעברה אצלו, see supra; and from

—3) to be extended, to be consolidated into one township. Yerushalmi Eruvin V, 22ᵇ bottom of page יכול אני … בית מעון מתעברת וכ׳ I can cause Beth Ma‘on and Tiberias to be considered one township (as regards Sabbath distances).

—4) to be added to, to be proclaimed a full month (of thirty days), a leap-year (of thirteen months). Yerushalmi Rosh Hashanah III, beginning 58ᶜ ניסן לא נ׳ מימיו Nisan was never made a full month (by decree of the court); Yerushalmi Sheviit X, beginning 39ᵇ; and e.—Sanhedrin 12ᵃ ראויה … שתִּתְעַבֵּר that year ought to have been a leap-year. Bava Metzia נִתְעַבְּרָה השנה נתע׳ לשוכר if the year was made a leap-year, the tenant (that rented by the year) reaps the benefit of the intercalation. Rosh Hashanah 19ᵇ; and from

Nifal - נֶעֱבַר (with עֲבֵרָה) to be committed. Tosefta Bava Kamma X, 3 בהמה ונֶעֶבְרָה בה עבירה if one stole a beast, and some sinful act was committed on it (by which it became forbidden for any benefit); (Bava Kamma IX, 2, and from נעבדה … עבירה).

לשם ששה דברים הזבח נזבח וכו' לשם ה' לשם מי שאמר והיה העולם. אף שבכל מקום מצינו שאמרו בביהמ"ק השוכן בבית הזה (מדות פ"ב,מ"ב) וכאן אמרו למי שאמר והיה העולם. ביאר בזה כ"ק אאמו"ר הגה"ק זללה"ה כי העולם הזה דומה לאכסדרה שמוקפת משלש רוחות ורוח צפונית אינה מסובבת כדאיתא (ב"ב כ"ה.) רוח צפונית הוא סטרא דשמאלא והוא הפתח אשר על ידו עבודת ישראל יסובבו אף סטרא שמאלא כדאיתא בזוה"ק (במדבר קע"ח:) ועבד הלוי הוא אשלים לסטר שמאלא הוא אשלים לפגימו דעלמא ואפילו האי סטרא דצפון דאשתאר חסר בעלמא כד ברא קוב"ה עלמא וזה שאומר לשם מי שאמר והיה העולם לימינא ולשמאלא שכן הציב השי"ת שסטר צפון יושלם ע"י עבודת ישראל וקרבנותיהן.
